content: A minimal RunVex clamp, useful for bounding a driven rig control (e.g. a corrective blendshape weight) so animators cannot push it out of its valid range.

code_blocks.code:

result = clamp(value, lo, hi);

content: smooth() is VEX's smoothstep: it eases a value with zero slope at both ends. In a rig it softens the response of a driven control so motion starts and stops gently.

code_blocks.code:
// APEX RunVex. Input: float t in [0,1]. Output: float result.
result = smooth(0.0, 1.0, t);

content: Starting from the identity, scale() then translate() mutate the matrix in place to build a TRS transform. Emitting it as a named matrix output lets downstream APEX nodes apply it to a joint or control.

content: fit() linearly remaps a value between input and output ranges -- the workhorse of driven-key style rigging, e.g. turning a slider's 0-10 range into a joint's -45..45 degrees.
title: Remap a Control Range (RunVex)

content: eulertoquaternion() converts per-axis euler angles into a single quaternion, which is the rotation form most APEX joint operations expect. The second argument selects the rotation order.

code_blocks.code:
// APEX RunVex. Input: vector euler (radians). Output: vector4 q.
q = eulertoquaternion(euler, 0);   // 0 = XYZ rotation order

title: Euler to Quaternion (RunVex)

prompt: Convert euler angles to a quaternion in APEX
explanation: eulertoquaternion() converts per-axis euler angles into a single quaternion, which is the rotation form most APEX joint operations expect. The second argument selects the rotation order.

content: Sampling noise at the shading position P gives a smooth 0-1 field that lerp() uses to mix two colours. Using world-space P keeps the pattern anchored to the object even under animation.

content: fit() remaps world height into 0-1 between the chosen bounds and clamp() keeps it in range past the limits. The result drives a vertical colour blend -- a building block for stratified rock, gradient backdrops and sky-style tints.

content: Centring the noise around zero (-0.5..0.5, scaled) gives a signed displacement so the surface pushes both in and out. Moving P along the normal is true geometric displacement; remember to recompute N or the shading will still reflect the original surface.

content: A cvex function declares its bound parameters in the signature; 'export' marks outputs the shading network reads back (here Cf). The body is an ambient-plus-lambert term against a fixed light direction -- the smallest complete shader you can compile with vcc.

content: Flooring the scaled UVs gives integer tile indices; the parity of their sum alternates 0/1 across the grid, producing a checker. It is the canonical UV-debug pattern and a base for tiled procedural textures.

explanation: Flooring the scaled UVs gives integer tile indices; the parity of their sum alternates 0/1 across the grid, producing a checker. It is the canonical UV-debug pattern and a base for tiled procedural textures.

content: length(v@v) is the per-particle speed; fit() normalises it against an expected maximum, and chramp() turns that into a colour. This is the fastest way to read sim energy at a glance and to tune solver settings.

content: The MPM solver tracks the elastic part of the deformation gradient; its determinant Je measures local volume change. abs(Je - 1) is a symmetric strain magnitude that highlights where the material is compressed or stretched -- useful for art-directing yield/fracture.
title: Colour MPM Particles by Elastic Strain
houdini_version_notes: f@Je (elastic volume ratio) is written per particle by the MPM Solver in Houdini 21; confirm the attribute name for your build.

explanation: The MPM solver tracks the elastic part of the deformation gradient; its determinant Je measures local volume change. abs(Je - 1) is a symmetric strain magnitude that highlights where the material is compressed or stretched -- useful for art-directing yield/fracture.

content: Normalising (P - center) gives an outward direction; multiplying by strength and f@TimeInc turns it into a per-substep velocity change that is independent of substep count. Clamping the distance avoids a divide-by-zero at the exact centre.

content: pcopen() opens a point cloud query around @P within a radius and pcnumfound() returns how many points it found. fit() inverts that count into a size, so crowded regions get small points and sparse regions get large ones. Always pcclose() the handle.

content: neighbours() returns the connected point indices; averaging their normals gives the local mean orientation. The dot product between that average and this point's normal is ~1 on flat areas and drops on curved areas, so 1 - dot is a handy curvature/edge-wear mask.

content: primpoints() gives the ordered points of each primitive. A first pass sums total length; a second pass writes the running fraction as curveu via setpointattrib(). Unlike the Resample SOP's curveu, this works without resampling and preserves the original points.

content: Each call to rand() with a distinct seed offset yields an independent stream, so orientation, scale and colour vary without correlating. quaternion(angle, axis) spins each copy about Y; fit01 maps the unit random into a size range.
